newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end sharply off on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end sharply off on profit-taking.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended sharply lower on Monday, hit by an afternoon slide in prices as a pause in the market's recent rally prompted investors to take profits.
The Hang Seng closed 125.61 points lower at 12,262.77. Turnover eased to HK$5.49 billion from HK$6.65 billion on Friday. The index is up three percent so far this month.
"Some of the profit-taking we have been expecting for four or five days is finally coming on stream," said Glenn Lesko, head of sales trading HG Asia.
"It (the Hang Seng) will probably stabilise around 12,200 and then we will wait for fresh external factors," he said.
Property stocks led Monday's decline as investors locked in gains following the sector's leading performance.
Shares in Henderson Land took the biggest hit, falling HK$0.82 to HK$68.00 as the stock went ex-dividend. Analysts said the move exaggerated the Hang Seng's slide.
Shares in Cheung Kong fell HK$1.00 to HK$60.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties slipped HK$1.00 to HK$85.00. However, Hysan Development bucked the trend and ended HK$0.10 higher at HK$24.30.
